name: Layered architecture
summary: Horizontal technical layers (presentation, business, persistence, database) in one deployable app. Closed layers keep changes inside one layer.
strengths: Simplest and cheapest style
Familiar to most developers
A fine starting point before the long-term direction is clear
weaknesses: A feature change touches every layer
Architecture sinkhole: requests pass through layers that add nothing
Scales and deploys only as a whole
Tends to erode into a big ball of mud
goodWhen: Small or simple apps and websites
Tight budget and schedule
Most changes are technical (swap UI framework or database)
avoidWhen: Large systems that need scalability, agility or frequent independent deployment

source.note: Style has a weak effect on security; neutral 3
One database with ACID transactions

name: Modular monolith
summary: One deployable app split into business-domain modules (orders, inventory, payments…), each with its own internal layers if needed.
strengths: Simple and cheap
Fits Domain-Driven Design; teams can own a module
Easy to evolve later into service-based or microservices
weaknesses: Needs strict governance or module boundaries erode
The whole app scales and deploys together
Technical changes (new UI or database tech) ripple across every module
goodWhen: Starting a new system, especially when its future direction is uncertain
Tight budget or time
avoidWhen: High scalability, availability or responsiveness needs

source.note: Style has a weak effect on security; neutral 3
One database with ACID transactions

name: Microkernel (plug-in) architecture
summary: A stable minimal core plus independent plug-ins for specialised, variable or customer-specific features, connected through a registry and contracts.
strengths: Easy to add, remove or customise features
Keeps messy custom logic out of the core
weaknesses: The core is a change bottleneck
goodWhen: Product-style software (IDEs, CI servers, issue trackers, browsers)
Lots of per-customer or per-region rule variation
avoidWhen: There is no real need for extensibility

source.note: Style has a weak effect on security; neutral 3
Mostly one database; remote plug-ins may hold their own data

name: Pipeline (pipes and filters)
summary: Data flows one way through independent processing steps (filters) linked by pipes.
strengths: Simple and cheap
Steps are reusable and easy to test on their own
weaknesses: Poor fit for interactive request/response apps
Limited scale and fault tolerance when deployed as one unit
goodWhen: ETL, media or data processing
Compilers, batch jobs, CI pipelines

name: Service-based architecture
summary: About 4–12 coarse-grained, separately deployed domain services, usually sharing one database.
strengths: Practical distribution at moderate cost
Good maintainability, testability and deployability
ACID transactions inside a service
goodWhen: Business apps with clear domains and moderate scale
A gradual move away from a monolith

source.note: Style has a weak effect on security; neutral 3
ACID inside a service; usually one shared database

name: Event-driven architecture
summary: Components react asynchronously to events through a broker (choreographed) or a mediator (orchestrated).
strengths: Very responsive, scalable and fault tolerant
Easy to add new reactions to existing events
weaknesses: Workflow state and error handling are hard
goodWhen: The business reacts to things happening
Async or parallel work; IoT, notifications, real-time flows

source.note: Style has a weak effect on security; neutral 3
Asynchronous messaging or replicated data means eventual consistency

name: Space-based architecture
summary: Processing units keep data in replicated in-memory grids; the database is updated asynchronously, outside the request path.
strengths: Top responsiveness, scalability and elasticity under huge, spiky load
weaknesses: Very complex, hard to test and expensive
goodWhen: Ticketing, auctions and flash sales, where a central database would choke
avoidWhen: Ordinary load; small teams; tight budgets

source.note: Style has a weak effect on security; neutral 3
Asynchronous messaging or replicated data means eventual consistency

name: Microservices
summary: Many small single-purpose services, each owning its data within a bounded context, deployed independently.
strengths: Top modularity, deployability and per-service testability
Top scalability and fault tolerance
Team autonomy
goodWhen: Clear bounded contexts and many teams
High scale and frequent independent releases
Mature operations

source.note: More endpoints but stronger isolation; neutral 3
Each service owns its data; cross-service work is eventually consistent

name: Orchestration-driven SOA
summary: Enterprise services coordinated through a central orchestration engine or enterprise service bus (ESB).
strengths: Large-scale enterprise integration
weaknesses: Everything is coupled to the bus
goodWhen: Existing enterprise integration landscapes

name: Serverless
summary: Functions (FaaS) and managed backend services (BaaS, e.g. managed auth, databases and storage) run by a cloud provider; pay per use; no servers to manage.
strengths: Scales automatically, down to zero and up to large bursts
No server operations
Cheap at low or spiky traffic
weaknesses: Vendor lock-in through provider-specific triggers and identity
Local testing and debugging are harder
goodWhen: Event-triggered tasks
Spiky or low traffic
Small teams that want no ops; MVPs on BaaS

name: Cell-based architecture
summary: The whole stack is copied into independent cells, each serving a subset of customers, behind a thin routing layer that uses a partition key.
strengths: Fault isolation: a failure affects one cell only
Predictable, testable maximum scale per cell
Scale by adding cells
weaknesses: Routing, cell-sizing, deployment and monitoring overhead
goodWhen: Large, critical multi-tenant platforms where limiting the blast radius matters

name: Peer-to-peer
summary: Nodes act as both clients and servers and share resources directly, with little or no central server.
strengths: Scales with the number of peers
No single point of failure
Low central infrastructure cost
goodWhen: File sharing, decentralised or blockchain apps
Local-first or offline collaboration
LAN multiplayer

name: Edge–cloud architecture
summary: Processing runs near the data source (devices, gateways, edge locations), with the cloud used for coordination, storage and heavy analytics.
strengths: Very low latency
Keeps working offline or on poor networks
Uses less bandwidth
weaknesses: Many devices to deploy, update and secure
Data sync and consistency are hard
goodWhen: Industrial IoT, retail stores, vehicles
AR/VR, video analytics on site
